data.headline: Damaged U.S. Jet’s Nearest Replacement Will Cost More Than $700 Million
data.summary: The E-3 Sentry jet damaged by an Iranian attack this week was part of a dwindling American fleet of early-warning aircraft with no easy replacements ready for service.  The jet serves as an airborne warning and control system aircraft, or Awacs, which can scan broad areas for friendly and enemy aircraft and missiles and help direct fire, acting as a nerve center for battles from the air.  The closest alternative, Boeing's E-7 Wedgetail, was projected to cost more than $700 million apiece last year when the Pentagon tried to cancel the program, only to revive it under congressional pressure.
